newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends ranged despite import covering.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends ranged despite import covering.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed flat againt the dollar on monday, despite commercial demand for the greenback, due to a high supply of the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 58.90 to the dollar, after briefly going to 58.91, they said.
"A state bank covered some imports, but it had hardly any impact on the market, which was well offered with dollars," said a HongKong Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 4.25 local cents on its overseas strength, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.8803 and 60.0698.
"I do not expect the dollar-rupee exchange rate to move much in the short-term, because the market seems to have enough dollars to cater to normal demand," said an American Express Bank dealer.
Overnight call money was at 8.875 percent with the market well offered, dealers said.
"The money market is also very well offered with two state banks lending," said the American Express Bank dealer. "Today we even saw six months money going at 12.5 percent."
The Central Bank's overnight repo rate is at 8.5 percent.
